subject: Decision Making
title: The Abilene Paradox
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Abilene Paradox.

hook.text: A Texas family drove 53 miles to Abilene in brutal heat for dinner. Afterward, nobody wanted to go.

buildup.text: Each person agreed to go because they thought the others wanted to. Nobody spoke their true preference.

discovery.text: The Abilene Paradox is collective agreement on something nobody actually wants. Groups do things no member supports.

twist.text: It is the opposite of groupthink. Groupthink suppresses dissent.

climax.text: Many meetings end with everyone agreeing to a plan nobody likes.

punchline.text: Everyone agreed. Nobody wanted to go. False consensus is silent and universal.

quiz.question: What is the Abilene Paradox?
options: A group agrees to something no individual member actually wants
